prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: game material texture atlas, not character concept art.
Create a square texture atlas divided into exactly FOUR equal square material tiles, a 2 by 2 grid with absolutely NO gutters, margins, borders, text or labels. Fill every pixel with material. Reference the worn hand-painted PS2 aesthetic and material colors in the supplied Cathedral Pilgrim turnaround. DO NOT include any person, body part, face, hand, arm, armor item, buckle, flask, strap, pouch, weapon, religious token or background in any tile. These are only flat surface materials for UV mapping to existing 3D geometry.
TOP LEFT tile: faded rusty RED wool cloak cloth, muted burnt red and brown, rough woven fibers, restrained painted folds and crease shadows, worn fabric, dirty weathering and subtle seam-like wear; broad low-contrast irregular material variation, no object silhouette and no holes.
TOP RIGHT tile: CHARCOAL gray-brown rough tunic fabric, sooty dark brown-gray, dirty and frayed woven textile, subtle vertical fold highlights and shadow creases, age spots and earthy grime. Preserve the concept's dark neutral cloth palette, no orange or green cloth.
BOTTOM LEFT tile: weathered BROWN leather, medium-dark umber, fine cracks, scuffs, creases and rubbed lighter grain, flat material only with no shaped clothing pieces, no stitching that makes it look like a complete pouch.
BOTTOM RIGHT tile: dirty BEIGE linen leg wrapping material, muted tan and cream cloth, low-contrast diagonal layered bandage lines, woven fiber, dirt, modest wear. Repeating wrap pattern with no human leg or anatomy.
Rendering: detailed hand-painted low-resolution early-2000s game texture aesthetic, slightly coarse texels, many subtle material colors and softly painted baked wear. NOT photorealistic macro photography, NOT polished smooth plastic, NOT Minecraft block noise, NOT a flat solid-color swatch. Lighting completely flat and diffuse, no directional cast shadows or highlights. Each tile should tile seamlessly within itself where possible. Tiles exactly meet at x=50% and y=50%.
